question: Does the finite-aggregation determinant-order transition survive finer starting-state grids and removal of the hard service threshold / best-partner update rule?

preserved.rng: collision-free SeedSequence hierarchy already fixed on 2026-09-22

grid_resolution_challenge.decision_rule: For every grid resolution, the winner by median component must be community at k=1, interaction at k=4, and starting state at k=16.
grid_resolution_challenge.rationale: Tests whether the reported C -> I -> S ordering is an artefact of the frozen 0.05 starting-state spacing.

rules.threshold_best: Frozen rule: if service < 0.45, move alpha toward the best-matching extant partner.
rules.smooth_weighted: No hard threshold and no best-partner switch: at every nonempty step move alpha*(1-service) toward the encounter-weighted centroid of extant partner traits.
rules.fixed: No plant-state movement; plant state remains at its initial value.

update_rule_challenge.primary_smooth_rule_decision: At least 4 of 6 seeds must have C>I at k=1 and I>C at one or more later k values under smooth_weighted feedback.
update_rule_challenge.fixed_rule_role: Negative-control description only; it is not required to pass or fail a directional criterion.

required: raw sum of squares for S, C and I at every rule/grid/k/seed
per-cell sum of squares for resolution-comparable magnitude
median raw and per-cell trajectories across seeds
log2 scaling slope of median per-cell SS against k
absolute_variance_reporting.interpretation: Normalized shares are not reported alone; the audit must reveal whether transient dominance accompanies growth, persistence or slower contraction of I relative to C.

claim_boundary: This is a post-freeze structural challenge. It may narrow the mechanistic interpretation if it fails, but it does not redefine the frozen Chapter 2 primary design, retune parameters, replace the collision-free headline receipt, or turn synthetic k into a calibrated natural quantity.
